statements.statement: NaN === NaN evaluates to true in TypeScript.
statements.explanation: NaN is not equal to anything, including itself. NaN === NaN is always false, which is why you need Number.isNaN() to check for it.
Number("hello") produces NaN because "hello" is not a valid number. Number.isNaN() correctly detects it.
42 is a valid number, not NaN. Number.isNaN() only returns true when the value is actually NaN.
